findings: The ribbon-corrupted known grid passes current input checks at 0.3675% disagreement while deviating 5.2525% from its latent clean weave. Input-mask agreement alone does not identify physical paper identity.
Correctly supplied ribbon uncertainty allows exact clean-mask recovery in this controlled grid. Hiding an unrelated border does not: its clean error rises to 6.259375%.

The real photograph retains distorted geometry in the unobserved ribbon region even when observed error falls to 0.250849%. There is no independently verified hidden template; no real-photo recovery claim.
The input crop, classified mask, and annotation regions stay fixed in all arms. Weighted inputs use the existing direct path while the unweighted arm can also try MILP.

All eight exports pass engine geometry and nominal-paper checks, convert to editable SVG, and pass editor intersection rules. None of the four real-photograph candidates passes all original full-mask checks.

visualReview.realFinding: Removing cap and ribbon observations reduces visible target disagreement but leaves pronounced central hooks and curved border extensions. This is not a clean recovered checker.
visualReview.syntheticFinding: The correctly masked ribbon control recovers the underlying checker; the unmasked and irrelevant-border variants retain ribbon-shaped distortions.

nextDiagnosis: The real both-unobserved candidate proposes 15 near-straight span reductions but rejects their batch on boundary_objective. Test continuous scoring per independent edit group without loosening final objective, source-feature, geometry or paper gates. This local cleanup cannot by itself establish the hidden design.

postFitAnnotationCorrection.finding: Later enlarged RGB review shows that the original vertical uncertainty polygon clips the ribbon's right edge. The claim that it conservatively covers the ribbon fringe is withdrawn. Original experiment inputs and results remain unchanged; they do not isolate a fully hidden ribbon.
